title: Non-Hermitian topological Euler insulators
abstract: Topological Euler insulators emerge in multiband systems with real Bloch Hamiltonians and wavefunctions. Their fragile topologies are characterized by the Euler class of degenerate bands and protected by the $PT$ or $C_2T$ symmetry in two dimensions, which go beyond the tenfold $K$-theory classification of topological matter. In this work, we extend the conception of topological Euler insulators to non-Hermitian systems and propose a theoretical framework to unlock their nontrivial Euler topology. Focusing on two-dimensional, three-band non-Hermitian lattice models with symmetric Hamiltonians, we formulate a comprehensive description of their topological Euler bands, entanglement spectrum and bulk-boundary correspondence. Three typical models of non-Hermitian Euler insulators are constructed and investigated explicitly to illustrate our theory. Unique topological phase transitions and anomalous edge-band overlaps with non-Hermitian origins are further identified. Our study establishes the presence of topological Euler bands in non-Hermitian systems and unveils their intriguing physical characteristics, thereby broadening the existing territory of topological matter in non-Hermitian open systems.
summary: This work generalizes the concept of topological Euler insulators to non-Hermitian systems, providing a theoretical framework to characterize their nontrivial topology. By analyzing three-band lattice models, the authors demonstrate that topological Euler bands persist in non-Hermitian regimes, revealing unique phase transitions and edge-band overlaps. This broadens the scope of topological matter theory into the realm of open quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper extends the concept of topological Euler insulators, characterized by the Euler class, from Hermitian to non-Hermitian quantum systems.
main_result: It establishes the existence of topological Euler bands in non-Hermitian systems and identifies non-Hermiticity-induced phase transitions and anomalous edge-band overlaps.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework using a generalized Euler class ($e_{12}$) and analyze the entanglement spectrum and bulk-boundary correspondence for non-Hermitian lattice models.
model_or_system: The focus is on two-dimensional, three-band non-Hermitian lattice models with symmetric Hamiltonians, described by a Bloch Hamiltonian $H(\mathbf{k})$.
key_observables: Topological Euler bands, entanglement spectrum, spectral gap ($\Delta$), and the Euler class ($e_{12}$).
important_parameters: The system is analyzed in gapped non-Hermitian phases ($\Delta > 0$).
main_assumptions: The theory is formulated for the three-band Hamiltonian but claims generalizability to multiple band systems.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, develops the theoretical framework using the Euler class and spectral diagnostics, applies it to construct and investigate three explicit non-Hermitian models, and concludes by discussing the physical implications.
why_interesting: The extension of topological invariants like the Euler class to non-Hermitian systems is crucial for understanding open quantum systems where gain/loss are present, bridging topological theory with open quantum dynamics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Spectral information of the Model I. (a) shows the spectral gap function ∆vs the real and imaginary parts of system parameter µ = µR + iµI. The value of ∆is trun- cated at 0.01, so that all regions with ∆≥0.01 are colored in yellow. The red solid lines are phase boundaries obtained from Eq. (37). (b) shows the spectrum of the system along the parameter line µI = µR in (a) under PBC. It is zoomed in around |E3| = 0 to show the gapped and gapless regions clearly. The gray area and blue solid line denote the bulk and lower edge of the highest band E3. Two other flat bands E1 and E2 at zero energy are not shown.

FIG. 2. Topological characterization of the Model I. (a) shows the real parts of Euler class e12 at different µ = µR + iµI [see Fig. 13(a) for the imaginary parts]. The values of e12 in different gapped phases are given explicitly. The red solid lines represent the analytically obtained phase boundaries in Fig. 1. (b)–(d) show the Wilson loop spectrum θy(kx) of the two degenerate bulk bands E1,2 vs kx for µI = 0.5.

FIG. 4. Bulk-boundary correspondence of the Model I. (a)– (d) show the absolute value of spectrum |E| with periodic and open boundary conditions taken along x and y directions, re- spectively. The system has Ny = 200 unit cells along the y direction. In each panel, the gray (blue and red) lines corre- spond to the spectra of bulk (edge) states.

FIG. 3. Entanglement spectrum of the Model I. The system has Ny = 100 unit cells along the y direction, and an equal bipartition is taken along y for evaluating the entanglement spectrum in each panel. In all panels, the gray (blue and red) lines are entanglement spectrum corresponding to bulk states (edge states generated along the entanglement cuts).

FIG. 5. Spectral information of the Model II. The system parameter is set as λ = 2 for both panels. (a) shows the spectral gap function ∆vs the real and imaginary parts of µ = µR + iµI. The value of ∆is truncated at 0.01, so that all regions with ∆≥0.01 are colored in yellow. The red solid lines are phase boundaries extracted numerically from Eq. (43). (b) shows the spectrum of the system along the parameter line µI = (3µR + 2)/7 in (a) under PBC. It is zoomed in around |E3| = 0 to show the gapped and gapless regions clearly. The gray area and blue solid line denote the bulk and lower edge of the highest band E3. Two other flat bands E1 and E2 at zero energy are not shown.
